title: Candidate chemistry and risk log — Calvin Torres
content:
Topline: rough, private notes on candidate X (interview loop 2024-09-17). Not polished — my impressions, quick heuristics, and follow-ups I want before the panel vote. Use for calibration; do not circulate externally.

Quick summary (1-sentence): Strong systems intuition and instincts about memory/KV cache tradeoffs, borderline on product sense for rollout constraints; medium hire risk because of sketchy open-source ops experience. Confidence: 6/10.

Signal highlights:
- Architecture sense: explicitly reasoned about KV cache eviction policies when multi-tenant models share GPU memory. Gave a concrete fallback flow (LRU + priority tiers) and explained latency tail trade-offs. Good sign for runtime work.
- Complexity comfort: comfortable sketching async batching pipelines end-to-end (client -> router -> batcher -> runtime), called out backpressure and retry semantics. Wanted to see a bit more on observability hooks but mentioned traces + per-token metrics.
- Communication: concise, draws helpful diagrams (used whiteboard effectively), translates tradeoffs into product implications (SLO vs cost).

Weak signals / concerns:
- Ops depth: when asked about debugging a memory leak in a quantized model server, answer pertained mostly to model code (PyTorch) rather than systems-level troubleshooting (nvprof, allocator traces, fragmentation). Has not owned cluster-level memory debugging end-to-end.
- OSS infra exposure: limited track record operating long-lived inference services. Most experience seems research-to-prototype, not multi-year production ownership.
- Scale assumptions: defaulted to single-region assumptions; didn't proactively address cross-region failover and cross-model routing (we care about region-aware routing policies).

Behavioral / collaboration notes:
- Proactive with design tradeoffs, asks clarifying questions early.
- Defensive when probed about gaps; framed unknowns as tradeoffs to learn vs risks to mitigate — good growth mindset.
- Willing to challenge PMs on unrealistic latency targets but open to compromise.

Interview-specific artifacts (my shorthand):
- Design prompt: "serve a 3B open model with 20k qps across multi-tenant customers; keep 95th <= 120ms"
  - Proposed: multi-tiered pool (hot, warm, cold), prefix cache, aggressive KV cache reuse, per-tenant rate-limits.
  - Missed: explicit admission control policy and how to migrate traffic during rollout with golden-traffic canary.

- Coding exercise: pseudo-code for continuous batcher + flush-on-timeout. Correct structure but had an edge-case bug (didn't handle duplicate request cancellation on client disconnect).

Scorecard (my private 1–5 scale):
- Technical depth (systems + infra): 3
- Runtime-specific heuristics (KV, batching, quantization awareness): 4
- Production ownership experience: 2
- Communication & cross-team: 4
- Role fit (senior staff vs senior IC): strong senior IC, marginal for Staff without grooming 1–2 yrs in ops.

Net recommendation: consider as "hire with onboarding plan" if team can pair on ops-first projects + shadow SRE for 3 months. Otherwise, high risk for a solo ops-heavy staff hire.

Open questions I want answered before panel vote:
1) Concrete production debugging story — ask for a specific incident where they diagnosed a memory fragmentation/allocator issue on GPUs; what tools, what timeline, what mitigations applied?
2) Ownership scope — have they ever been the primary on-call owner for a model-serving fleet? For how long and what was their escalation playbook?
3) Rollout example — ask for a 3-step canary migration they ran (tools, metrics watched, rollback criteria).

Suggested follow-ups for interview loop / hiring manager:
- Small take-home: give a 90-minute scenario: "You see 99th latency spike after a model update — walk through debugging steps and mitigation plan." Listen for use of observability instrumentation and incremental mitigations (throttling, fallback to smaller model, scaled replicas).
- Optional pairing: pair with SRE for a short session to probe ops instincts.

Potential red flags to track if hired:
- Tendency to treat model-level fixes as the first option instead of systems mitigations. Can be costly in orgs where model changes require long cycles.
- Limited history owning long-running services at scale — may need explicit mentorship.

Notes to self (action items):
- Draft 3 clarifying questions to send to hiring manager (Jodi) by 2024-09-19.
- If backchannel checks (refs) are positive on ops ownership, move to hire-with-plan. If refs show only short-lived prototypes, vote = no.

Scratch heuristics (for calibration across other candidates):
- If candidate scores <=3 on production ownership and >=4 on systems heuristics, they can be a fast-impact IC but not yet a Staff owner.
- Look for explicit examples with timelines: "I was primary on-call for X for Y months" vs vague "I supported ops".

Bottom line: leaning towards green-hire for senior IC with onboarding; do not recommend direct hire for Staff-level without stronger ops evidence.

Raw, unedited — Calvin
